issues.title: Fast sandbox ingress POC: raw file reference + MoE large-model execution
issues.body:
## Goal
Reduce one-shot large-model validation wall-clock time in ChatGPT sandbox. Model changes are allowed if they materially improve end-to-end speed; do not optimize for repeated inference.

## Execution contract
Canonical one-shot TCC plan:
- `docs/TCC_ONE_SHOT_SANDBOX_LLM_PLAN_2026-10-02.md`
- `docs/TCC_ONE_SHOT_SANDBOX_LLM_PLAN_2026-10-02.json`

These documents are authoritative for branch order, retries, stop conditions, environment separation, and closure reporting. No manual mid-run tuning is permitted.

## Hard environment rule
- GPT sandbox is the default execution environment.
- Mac is forbidden except tests intrinsically requiring physical hardware or OS-specific device I/O.
- Audio-file ASR/accuracy/performance tests run in GPT sandbox only.
- GitHub Actions remain disabled.

## Current findings
- GitHub text-shard ingress is verified but incurs Base64 expansion and connector/tool-call overhead.
- Generic Binary Ingress MCP server-side fetch is already qualified for Qwen2.5-0.5B (397,808,192 bytes, exact SHA), but current Plus attachment is blocked by ChatGPT custom MCP product access.
- MCP resource `blob` is Base64 on the ChatGPT boundary, so MCP alone does not eliminate transfer expansion.
- Google Drive connector supports raw-file streaming with `download_raw_file=true` and `include_base64=false`, returning a file reference that can be materialized into the sandbox. This is the highest-priority ingress path to benchmark.
- For large-model execution, large MoE is preferred where semantically acceptable because total capacity can remain high while active parameters remain low.
- llama.cpp lazy/on-demand expert paging and mmap are runtime candidates when model size exceeds practical sandbox RAM.

## TCC route order
1. Connector-native raw file reference -> sandbox materialize.
2. Generic Binary Ingress if directly attachable end-to-end.
3. GitHub Base64 text shards fallback.

## TCC model/runtime order
1. Large MoE candidate supported by current runtime.
2. Required large dense model if MoE is not semantically acceptable.
3. Small model only as control/smoke; never substitute it for a required large-model result.

Runtime branch:
- model file > 75% available RAM: lazy/expert-paging if available, else mmap;
- model file <= 75% available RAM: mmap first;
- OOM/kill: one retry with lazy/expert-paging, then reject candidate;
- runtime incompatibility: next predeclared compatible runtime/candidate.

## One-shot gates
P0 Preflight -> P1 Ingress -> P2 Runtime Strategy -> P3 Smoke -> P4 Full LLM Assay -> P5 Sandbox Audio Validation -> P6 Selection -> TCC Closure.

Only independent preflight/evidence checks may run concurrently. Any branch changing route/model/runtime is sequential and authority-bound.

## Decision rule
A candidate is admissible only if ingress integrity, smoke, frozen-assay integrity, correctness threshold, and sandbox resource gates all pass.

Select the admissible candidate with minimum:
`TOTAL_WALL_CLOCK = ingress + materialize/reconstruct + model-open + full-assay execution + scoring`

Tie-breakers:
1. fewer external->sandbox calls;
2. lower peak RSS;
3. lower transferred bytes;
4. simpler mainline runtime.

## Terminal states
- PASS_SELECTED
- NO_ADMISSIBLE_MODEL
- INVALID_TEST_CONTRACT
- TRANSPORT_BLOCKED
- SANDBOX_RESOURCE_LIMIT
- MAC_REQUIRED_FOR_PHYSICAL_TEST_ONLY

## Closure requirement
One final report only: selected route/model/runtime, exact branch path, timings/resources, correctness/audio metrics, rejected candidates and reasons, uncrossed blockers, hashes/versions, and next action only if no admissible configuration exists.

issues.title: Phase1 v2 EC binding — resolved with scoped incompatibility terminal
issues.body:
## Resolution

Actual ECv4.4 binding and provenance qualification are complete, but the frozen Phase1 S3/S4 abstraction is not fully isomorphic to EC-native semantics.

Canonical evidence:
- `results/phase1_ecv44_reframe_actual_2026-10-03.json` — actual EC-native reframing 9/10.
- `results/phase1_ecv44_s3_native_interface_compatibility_2026-10-03.json` — native next-action authority is singleton; frozen S3 admissible-set selection is not isomorphic.
- `results/phase1_s4_identifiability_audit_2026-10-03.json` — frozen S3 does not identify S4 closure.
- `results/ec_native_adapter_qualification.json` — scoped authority classification.
- `results/phase1_mvp_tcc_v2_actual_2026-10-03.json` — terminal `EC_NATIVE_SCOPE_INCOMPATIBLE`.

The original goal of a reportable EC S1-S4 baseline cannot be truthfully completed under the frozen generic contract without changing semantics. That incompatibility is now an experimental result rather than a missing implementation.

Successor research is tracked by the function-boundary protocol; the frozen Phase1 result remains unchanged. GitHub Actions remain disabled and Google Drive model relay remains unused.

issues.title: Phase1 MVP: freeze materiality and capacity-ambiguity decision thresholds before measurement
issues.body:
## Resolution
Frozen before any new ~0.5B measurement result is inspected.

Canonical contracts:
- `docs/PHASE1_MVP_AC_DEPENDENCY_TCC_2026-10-03.md`
- `docs/PHASE1_MVP_AC_DEPENDENCY_TCC_2026-10-03.json`

## Frozen operational rules
- Oracle-substitution-gain materiality: absolute >= 0.20.
- S3/S4 LLM-vs-EC joint-layer difference materiality: absolute >= 0.20 with identical upstream hashes.
- One-fixture 0.10 movement: non-material for dominant-layer selection.
- Material-layer gains within 0.10: `MVP_AMBIGUOUS_DOMINANT_LAYER`; no manual tie break.
- No material layer: `MVP_NO_MATERIAL_LAYER`.
- ~1.5B branch is authorized exactly once only when the schema-constrained ~0.5B arm is valid but decision-family collapse is present: oracle >=2 classes, model mode share >=0.90, family accuracy <=0.60.
- Output-contract failure is `INVALID_LLM_OUTPUT_CONTRACT`, not a capacity escalation.
- No automatic 4B escalation.

These thresholds are operational MVP rules, not statistical-significance claims. They are now immutable for `PHASE1_MVP_TCC_V1`; any methodology change requires a new protocol version.

issues.title: Phase1 S1/S2 + A/B/E runner — superseded by function-boundary successor
issues.body:
## Resolution

The frozen Phase1-v2 successor TCC now terminates at `EC_NATIVE_SCOPE_INCOMPATIBLE` before the old full A/B/E downstream implementation is required.

Reason:
- S3 all-admissible-set selection is not isomorphic to EC native singleton next-action authority.
- Frozen S3 does not identify generic S4 closure.
- Fabricating an EC B arm with harness-local semantics would violate the EC-native provenance contract.

Therefore this issue's original full A/B/E acceptance criteria are no longer valid for the frozen protocol. Do not create placeholder runners to satisfy them.

The still-relevant upstream research — discriminative S1 semantic extraction, S2 candidate recall, and shared-subfunction comparisons — is moved into the versioned `EC_LLM_FUNCTION_BOUNDARY_2026_10_03_V1` successor tracked separately.

Canonical evidence:
- `docs/EC_LLM_FUNCTION_BOUNDARY_2026-10-03.md`
- `results/ec_llm_function_boundary_2026-10-03.json`
- `results/phase1_mvp_tcc_v2_actual_2026-10-03.json`

GitHub Actions remain disabled.

issues.title: Phase1 MVP: add oracle-blind EC-native S3/S4 adapter before claiming actual ECv4.4
issues.body:
## Discovered by AC/dependency audit on 2026-10-03

The Phase1 generic S3/S4 artifact contract does not directly match the production/research ECv4.4 runtime contract.

Verified ECv4.4 components at pinned commit `d5ec423968f1c9242c590e5e77ccfd92d1f59eb2`:
- `ec_residual_detector.py` — residual detection (`EC_V4_4_RESIDUAL_DETECTOR_V1`)
- `ec_framing_search.py` — bounded intent-preserving framing search (`EC_V4_4_FRAMING_SEARCH_V1`)
- `v4_4_control.py` — remediation-plan next-action control (`EC_V4_4_CONTROL_PLANE_V1`)
- `atomic_closure_mode.py` — EC run-state closure engine

The current Phase1 runner selects generic candidate IDs with harness-local `select_candidates()` and makes closure decisions with harness-local `closure_decision()`. Binding only `ec_residual_detector` is therefore insufficient to label the entire S3/S4 result as actual ECv4.4.

## Blocking methodological rule
Do not force EC-native workflow semantics into generic candidate selection by silently changing the meaning of the fixture. Add one explicit, versioned, deterministic, oracle-blind adapter layer and qualify it before reportable EC measurements.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Define `PHASE1_EC_NATIVE_ADAPTER_V1` mapping frozen Phase1 v2 generic artifacts to EC-native inputs without reading any hidden/oracle fields.
2. Adapter consumes only model-visible task + persisted target-layer upstream artifacts.
3. Map S3 reframing to actual `detect_residuals/search_framing` and record both protocols/module SHAs.
4. For S3 selection, either:
   a. construct a semantics-preserving EC remediation-plan representation and use actual `V44ControlPlane.select_next_action`, with a deterministic reverse mapping to candidate IDs; or
   b. explicitly mark generic candidate selection `EC_NATIVE_NOT_APPLICABLE` and remove any claim that ECv4.4 itself performed that subfunction.
   No harness-local rule may be mislabeled as ECv4.4.
5. Map S4 closure to the actual EC closure authority only when the frozen fixture can be represented without oracle information; otherwise mark that subfunction `EC_NATIVE_NOT_APPLICABLE` rather than simulate it.
6. Adapter round-trip/identity tests prove no hidden evaluation field is consumed and upstream hashes remain unchanged.
7. Each reportable result states per subfunction implementation authority: `EC_NATIVE`, `ADAPTER`, `NOT_APPLICABLE`; no mixed result may be summarized simply as `actual ECv4.4` without this provenance.
8. If the generic abstraction is incompatible with EC-native semantics for a subfunction, treat incompatibility as an experimental finding, not an implementation defect to be hidden.
9. GitHub Actions remain disabled.

## Dependency
Blocks Issue #20 closure and reportable EC S3/S4 baseline. Must be included in the Phase1 MVP TCC DAG.

issues.title: Phase1 Oracle intervention E arm — superseded by scoped function-boundary protocol
issues.body:
## Resolution

`PHASE1_ORACLE_INTERVENTION_V1` remains a valid causal intervention design, but the frozen full S1-S4 A/B/E program is no longer executable as originally defined because Phase1-v2 terminates at `EC_NATIVE_SCOPE_INCOMPATIBLE`.

Do not mutate the frozen protocol to force S3 admissible-set selection or S4 generic closure into EC-native semantics.

Any future Oracle intervention is applied only inside a successor subfunction experiment where the compared function is genuinely shared and its upstream interface is identifiable.

Canonical successor:
- `docs/EC_LLM_FUNCTION_BOUNDARY_2026-10-03.md`
- `results/ec_llm_function_boundary_2026-10-03.json`

The existing intervention contract is retained as design evidence, not an open blocker. GitHub Actions remain disabled.
